name: Change
description: Sorts a code turn by kind of change and gives each route its context and route checks; every leaf is one of the hook's five labels

kind.label: What kind of code change is this?

config.instructions: The user's prompt (state.prompt) asks for a code change in SequenceTree, a C++ JUCE plugin. What kind of code change does state.prompt ask for?

options.label: Restructure existing code without changing what it does: extract, inline, rename, move, reorder, split or merge functions or classes
Change only layout, naming, ordering, grouping or formatting
Fix a bug, or add or change what the code does

scope.label: How far does the refactor reach?

config.instructions: How far does the refactor state.prompt asks for reach?

options.label: Inside one or a few functions
Across a class or several classes: members moved, a class split or merged, ownership changed
Anything the audio thread, processBlock, TraversalLogic or the modulator walk reaches

audio.label: Does it touch the audio thread?

config.statement: The change state.prompt asks for touches the audio thread, the traversal, MIDI timing, or anything processBlock calls.

config.description: Code change with the design-rule and readability gates.
config.directive: Write the change under the Key Design Rules; the design-rule and readability gates check it when the turn ends.
config.context: Refactor turn. Extracts, inlines and renames go through `refactor.encap`, `refactor.decap` and `refactor.replace`, and multi-site rewrites through `refactor.rewrite`; read the command's section of ~/Documents/GitHub/research-suite/REFACTORING.md before using it.

config.description: Code change with the design-rule and readability gates.
config.directive: Write the change under the Key Design Rules; the design-rule and readability gates check it when the turn ends.
config.context: Refactor turn. Extracts, inlines and renames go through `refactor.encap`, `refactor.decap` and `refactor.replace`, and multi-site rewrites through `refactor.rewrite`; read the command's section of ~/Documents/GitHub/research-suite/REFACTORING.md before using it. Run `refactor.order` on every file whose definitions moved, and `refactor.smell` on the directories touched.

config.description: Full protocol: gates plus the systematic pass.
config.directive: Run the full verification protocol: front-load api-surface, structure and data-flow before editing, and end with the SYSTEMATIC PASS block.
config.context: Traversal refactor. Every walk is the same traversal: run the walk-parity shapes in Tests/TraversalTests.cpp, and add one for any mechanic the change touches.

config.description: Code change with the design-rule and readability gates.
config.directive: Write the change under the Key Design Rules; the design-rule and readability gates check it when the turn ends.
config.context: Style turn. The grouping, initializer-list, argument-wrapping and hierarchy-order rules are the Project Design Rules; run `readability.sh --file` on each file you change.

config.description: Full protocol: gates plus the systematic pass.
config.directive: Run the full verification protocol: front-load api-surface, structure and data-flow before editing, and end with the SYSTEMATIC PASS block.
config.context: Audio-thread change: no allocation, lock or message post is reachable from processBlock; verify with SequenceTree_RealtimeTests if the change reaches it.
